item.title: Toyota Publica 1200SR (1971)
item.description:
Publication: Car Graphic
Format: Road Impression
Date: June 1971
Author: Shotaro Kobayashi

Road-testing the Toyota Publica 1200SR

Over the past six months, C/G has tested three versions each of the Publica and Sunny. This is partly because new models appear so frequently, but more importantly, because these least expensive offerings from the two major manufacturers—particularly their sporting models—provide the most performance at the lowest cost, and have won the support of a broad range of buyers (by no means limited to young people) as basic transportation for the enthusiast.

item.title: Toyota Publica 1200SR, Corolla 1400SR, and Sprinter 1400SR (1971)
item.description:
Publication: Motor Fan
Format: Test Drive Report
Date: June 1971
Author: Hiroshi Okazaki, Harukuni Takahashi, Motor Fan Editorial Staff (uncredited)

Does the “SR” Hit the Mark for the Performance-Minded?

We took Toyota’s new SR series out onto a rally course and drove the cars hard. Our team (appearing as “A,” “B,” “C,” and “D”) was a mix of professional drivers and members of the Motor Fan editorial staff. “Not quite enough for serious rally competition, but hard to fault as a ’town sport’"—that was our conclusion. (Skip to Publica 1200SR…)

item.title: Toyota Publica 1200ST and 1971 Publica 1200SR (1972)
item.description:
Publication: Motor Fan
Format: “Photorama” Test Drive report
Date: April 1972
Author: Kazuhiko Mitsumoto

An Almost Too-Good “Beat Machine”

“The Publica has completely lost every trace of the days when it was hailed as the ‘People’s Car,’” says Mitsumoto. With the new Publica transformed from a practical utility car into something altogether more stylish, the Photorama series makes another appearance.

New Publica 1200ST (Young Series)

“New Styling, New Publica—Now in Two Series” is the advertising line. The two series, it seems, are divided into “Family” and “Young,” with the Young Series in particular promoted as having been “created by Toyota’s young power, with young people in mind.” Whatever the product, all this fuss about “young people” and “youth” in advertising is really aimed at getting young people to part with the money they have saved up. Statistics apparently show that unmarried people between the ages of 24 and 27 have the highest rate of savings.

item.title: Toyota Publica 1200XL (1972)
item.description:
Publication: Motor Fan
Format: “Bubble Index” Road Test
Date: April 1972
Authors: Osamu Mochizuki, Katsuzo Kageyama, Shigeki Asaoka, Yasuhei Oguchi, Reiko Ikuuchi, Kensuke Ishizu

Will It Become the Leading Player of the “My Car” Age?

The third-generation Publica, now in its second model change, won considerable praise for its powertrain and performance. At the same time, it once again poses the question to users: “What should a mass-market car be?”
